# nonNumberLike

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** convertible to a number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNumberLike() — Checks whether a value is **not** convertible to a number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/base</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonNumberLike(value: unknown): boolean;
```

`nonNumberLike(value)` is the same test as `!isNumberLike(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

A finite number, or a string that converts to one. `NaN`, the infinities and the empty string are excluded, which is what separates this from a bare `Number(value)`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type      | Description         |
| :-------- | :-------- | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `unknown` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not convertible to a number; otherwise `false`.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonNumberLike(NaN); // => true
nonNumberLike(Infinity); // => true
nonNumberLike(""); // => true
nonNumberLike(null); // => true
nonNumberLike(1); // => false
nonNumberLike("1.5"); // => false
nonNumberLike(" 42 "); // => false
```
